title: Build a read-only Exchange mailbox report
summary: Which of six pretend mailboxes should appear on a list for people and shared teams? You can build the report without connecting to a mail system.
requires: Get the offline practice kit and PowerShell 7. You can run the included answer without Devin or a mail connection. To build with Devin, also use an approved practice repository. The optional actual mail check needs separate permission.
features: Ask Devin for a plan. Read its script. Use pretend mailbox rows and a small test to check the result.
roles: Make a read-only mailbox list.
Share a report someone else can test.
Build a small tool with a known answer.
prompt: Plan Get-MailboxInventory.ps1 for PowerShell 7. In practice mode use -InputCsv. In live mode use -Live in an already signed-in session. Both need -OutputCsv for a new file. Read only user and shared mailboxes. Keep DisplayName, PrimarySmtpAddress and RecipientTypeDetails, in that order. Sort by the main mail address. Preserve commas and accents. With no matches, write only the header. Stop for a blank or repeated address, an existing output, or a failed read. Keep any old file safe. In live mode use only Get-EXOMailbox -RecipientTypeDetails UserMailbox,SharedMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited -ErrorAction Stop. Show how each rule will be tested.

steps.title: Unzip the sample kit
steps.text: Tap Download the practice kit. Unzip it. Find the folder holding mailboxes.csv. Open PowerShell 7 there and run the three lines. Predict which four of the six rows will be included.
steps.help: Get-Location shows the current folder. If the CSV is missing, look inside the unpacked folder. The room and device rows stay out.
steps.code:
Get-Location
$PSVersionTable.PSVersion
Import-Csv ./mailboxes.csv | Format-Table -AutoSize

steps.title: Open a practice project
steps.text: Save mailboxes.csv and Test-Inventory.ps1 in an approved practice repository on a new branch. Keep the Reference folder on your computer. In Devin choose that project, open Ask and paste the opening prompt.
steps.help: Ask Devin to name the two files it sees. If you have no Devin access, use the Reference script on your computer starting at the next-but-one step.

steps.title: Move from a plan to a script
steps.text: Read the plan. Check which mailbox types it will read and what it will do if a read fails. Use Send to Devin or start an Agent session in the same project. Give it the request.
steps.help: Look at the changed files. You expect one report script. If there are extra mail commands, ask what they do before running the file.
steps.code: Write Get-MailboxInventory.ps1 from the plan. Run the tests if PowerShell 7 is available. Make a draft pull request so I can review the change. Show the changed file, test command, results and any part you could not test.

steps.title: Make a local report
steps.text: Place the reviewed script beside the practice CSV. These lines run the included answer. To test your own script, set $reportScript to its path first. Open the resulting rows with Import-Csv.
steps.help: Use a fresh output name if report.csv already exists. Team, Blue is one field. Quoted commas belong inside that field.
steps.code:
$reportScript = './Reference/Get-MailboxInventory.ps1'
& $reportScript -InputCsv ./mailboxes.csv -OutputCsv ./report.csv
Import-Csv ./report.csv | Format-Table -AutoSize

steps.title: Run the five checks
steps.text: Run the test file in the same PowerShell window. Read each result. It checks which rows appear, the header with no rows, bad addresses, an existing output and a pretend live read.
steps.help: Five PASS lines mean the script met the practice checks. The test uses a stand-in for Exchange, so it can run without a mail connection.
steps.code: ./Test-Inventory.ps1 -Script $reportScript

steps.title: Prove the test can catch a mistake
steps.text: Run the block. It makes a temporary copy of the answer, reverses the sort there and tests that copy. Then it removes the temporary file and checks the original again.
steps.help: Look for a failed order check on the temporary copy. The untouched answer should still pass. This shows the test can catch a real difference.
steps.code:
$copy = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("inventory-{0}.ps1" -f [guid]::NewGuid())
(Get-Content ./Reference/Get-MailboxInventory.ps1 -Raw).Replace('Sort-Object PrimarySmtpAddress |', 'Sort-Object PrimarySmtpAddress -Descending |') | Set-Content -LiteralPath $copy
try { ./Test-Inventory.ps1 -Script $copy } catch { $_.Exception.Message } finally { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $copy }
./Test-Inventory.ps1 -Script ./Reference/Get-MailboxInventory.ps1

steps.title: Optional: run an approved live read
steps.text: The local exercise is complete. For a live check, use only a work computer and account approved for this read. Open a fresh PowerShell 7 window with the approved Exchange module. Inspect the script first. Sign in on that computer only, then use the commands.
steps.help: The live script reads mailboxes your account may see. It writes a local CSV to a fresh path. Keep that file on the approved device. Never paste it into the agent or add it to the practice project.

steps.title: Review the evidence
steps.text: Read the code, the five test results and the list of changed files. For an approved live run, check one user mailbox and one shared mailbox in your admin center. Keep a short note of the command and counts.
steps.help: Label your results clearly. A simulated live read proves the code followed the test rules. An actual sign-in is a different test.

check: The four addresses sort as accounts@example.test, box-a@example.test, box-b@example.test and box-c@example.test. The types in order are shared, user, shared, user.
All five checks pass with the original. The backward sort fails. Team, Blue stays in one name field and Café Desk keeps its accent. Room and device rows stay out.

title: Capstone: ship a two-player treasure hunt
summary: Finish and test a local game with turns, hidden tiles, a score and a clear end.
requires: Open Devin with access to an approved practice repository. A repository is the project folder with its saved history. Use a separate practice branch, a copy where you can try changes.
features: A fixed board lets two people check the same scores. Hiding a used tile again during a round would make the proof fall apart.
roles: Use a fixed sample to replay a mail incident.
Design a reproducible two-team drill.
Ship a complete local treasure game.
prompt: Build a browser game with six covered buttons, a visible turn, totals, replay and a short help page. In test mode keep this grid fixed. A used tile cannot consume another turn. End after six legal picks. Include tests and a README for a fresh reader.

steps.title: Start a practice session
steps.text: Open the practice repository in Devin. Give the agent the sample. A session is one job and its conversation.
steps.help: Check the repository name on the session before giving it the lab request.
steps.code: Fixed 2×3 grid slots 1–6 contain coin, blank, coin, gem, blank, coin. Coin=1, gem=3. Turns alternate Blue then Gold.

steps.text: Send the lab request. Ask Devin to run the sample in its practice workspace and show the file and test output. Open the file preview or change view.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Open the browser preview or run the app from its README on your computer. Try the sample actions. Pick 1, then 4, then 1 again. Blue has 1 and Gold 3. The repeat leaves Blue’s turn in place.
steps.help: Follow the six legal picks on paper. Leave the repeated pick off your turn list. Give the gem three points and each coin one.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Continue with 2, 3, 5 and 6. Read the winner and replay. Test all buttons with the keyboard.
steps.help: If the winner differs, write down who owned each legal pick and check whether the repeated 1 wrongly used a turn.

check: Pick 1, then 4, then 1 again. Blue has 1 and Gold 3. The repeat leaves Blue’s turn in place.
The final scores are Blue 1 and Gold 5. Replay covers all six tiles and returns the first turn to Blue.

title: Capstone: deliver a read-only mail change desk
summary: Combine a before-and-after report, a download and a test that protects a good result.
requires: Open Devin with access to an approved practice repository. A repository is the project folder with its saved history. Use a separate practice branch, a copy where you can try changes.
features: Two snapshots tell you which rows changed. A bad snapshot can make an entire group seem to vanish, so check both lists first.
roles: Review a fake mailbox type change.
Compare two saved inventory lists.
Build a tool that shows exactly what changed.
prompt: Build a local HTML app with two CSV inputs, Compare, a visible check table and Download report. Label Added, Removed, Type changed and Same. Validate each file for unique nonblank IDs and known types before updating. Include samples, README, and a test for a bad second file. Use no mail connection.

steps.text: Open the practice repository in Devin. Give the agent the sample. A session is one job and its conversation.

steps.code: Before A=user, B=shared, C=user. After A=user, B=user, D=shared. IDs are pretend and match without case.

steps.title: Ask for a working result
steps.text: Send the lab request. Ask Devin to run the sample in its practice workspace and show the file and test output. Open the file preview or change view.
steps.help: If it only describes what should happen, ask for a run on the supplied rows. If the tool is missing, ask for the exact command to run in your own practice folder.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Open the browser preview or run the app from its README on your computer. Try the sample actions. The clean run shows D added, C removed, B changed from shared to user and A the same. Every ID appears once.
steps.help: Match the two A rows and the two B rows before checking for additions or removals. Read the type on each side of B to spot the change.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Save the good report. Add a second b to After and compare. Then restore the original input and download again.
steps.help: If B and b become separate boxes, check each ID after cleaning spaces and case but before building the comparison.

check: The clean run shows D added, C removed, B changed from shared to user and A the same. Every ID appears once.
The duplicate case shows a row error and keeps the last good result. The restored download matches all four expected entries.
